description:
MEASURED s459am, which is what #862 asked for ("RE-MEASURE the `slices` bench
row before spending anything on ARM B").
ARM A shipped and is worth what it promised on its own shape: the new `feread`
bench row (a read-only `for my $x (@a)` over a 1000-element array, the exact
program #862 quotes) went 0.71x perl -> 0.47x, PCL 0.3970 s -> 0.2746 s, an
A/B in one session through the arm's own Kind-A gate.
`slices` did NOT move: 3.02x with the arm OFF, 3.06x with it ON (perl 0.100 /
0.069, PCL 0.303 / 0.210 -- the two runs' perl sides differ more than the
arm does, i.e. the difference is load, not the transform).
So the promotion arm contributes ~nothing to `slices`, which CONFIRMS s458ak's
sb-sprof reading (neither make-p-box nor the promotion arm appears in its top
19) from the other direction.  ARM B as #862 scopes it -- "skip the promotion
in a slice COPY position" -- is therefore optimizing something that is not in
the profile.
RECOMMENDATION: close ARM B as scoped, and if `slices`' remaining ~3x is worth
attacking, re-file it against what the profile actually says is there: the
equal-hash lookups (21 %), p-array-fill's own construction, and the key
stringify.  That is a different piece of work with a different design, not a
boxing question.
  RATIFIED s459f (Fable, 2026-08-31): ARM B CLOSED by measurement -- the slices row's remaining ~3x is equal-hash lookups / p-array-fill construction / key stringify, a different design question; anyone attacking it re-files against the profile, never as a boxing arm.  Fable's own probes on the merged tree: 11-row battery, 10 SAME (the one DIFF is #810's pre-existing literal-list read-only half, untouched by ARM A and correctly revoked from the raw arm).
